title: Computer-aided polyp detection raised adenoma detection by non-experts in a trial
summary: In a randomised, non-inferiority trial (AID-2; NCT04260321) of 660 patients examined by 10 non-expert endoscopists, adenoma detection rate was 53.3% with computer-aided detection versus 44.5% in controls (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.04-1.40). The authors compared this with an earlier trial in expert endoscopists. A commercial system was evaluated and the outcome is a surrogate.
ai_technology: Commercial computer-aided polyp detection (CADe) during colonoscopy
organization: Humanitas University; Humanitas Clinical and Research Center IRCCS

evidence.tested: Prospective randomised controlled trial of 660 patients.
evidence.unknown: Effects on interval cancer or other long-term outcomes are not stated; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: AI polyp detection assisted endoscopists during colonoscopy.
